chain.title: Turn Up Some Bait
chain.desc: Worms go in your rod's bait slot and make fish bite sooner. They are consumed as you fish, so you want a running supply rather than a single one.

chain.title: Stop Digging For Worms
chain.desc: Feed it compostable scraps and it breeds worms for you. Build one early; it ends the tedious part of the mod permanently.

chain.title: A Rod That Takes Attachments
chain.desc: The mod's own rod, and the thing every other item plugs into: it has slots for a hook, bait, a fishing line and a bobber, which a vanilla rod does not.

chain.title: The First Hook
chain.desc: Fitted to your rod it gives a 20% chance a cast costs no durability. It is also the blank that every fancier hook is crafted on top of, so make several.

chain.title: Start Filleting
chain.desc: Put a fish and a knife together in the crafting grid to cut the fish into fillets. Without a knife the mod's thirty-odd fish species are mostly dead weight.

chain.title: Meat From The Catch
chain.desc: The universal output of filleting: every species becomes the same raw fillet, so one food chain covers your whole catch.

chain.title: Cook The Fillets
chain.desc: Furnace, smoker or campfire turns raw fillets into a proper meal. This is the food you will actually live on while fishing.

chain.title: A Knife That Survives The Day
chain.desc: The wooden knife dies after a handful of fish. Iron lasts long enough to process a full trip's catch in one sitting.

chain.title: Sushi
chain.desc: A raw fillet wrapped in seagrass. Worth knowing because it needs no fuel, so you can eat on a boat far from any furnace.

chain.title: Somewhere To Keep The Tackle
chain.desc: A block that stores whole rods together with spare hooks, bait, lines and bobbers, and is where you fit attachments onto a rod. One is enough.

chain.title: Dress The Line
chain.desc: A dyeable attachment for the rod's line slot. It is cosmetic, so one is plenty unless you want a second colour.

chain.title: A Bobber Of Your Own
chain.desc: The other dyeable attachment, sitting in the bobber slot. Like the line it changes how your cast looks, not how it fishes.

chain.title: Lucky Hook
chain.desc: Carries a luck modifier that biases what you reel in toward treasure. This is the hook to wear when you are hunting for boxes rather than food.

chain.title: Two At A Time
chain.desc: Two iron hooks welded together give a chance to land two catches from one cast. The best throughput hook before diamond.

chain.title: Something Heavy On The Line
chain.desc: The rarest thing in the junk pool - one weight against a Box's six and a Lockbox's four. Open it for an iron ingot, gold, a diamond or an emerald, so it is the richest of the three containers you can fish up.

chain.title: The Rod That Lasts
chain.desc: The best craftable rod short of neptunium, and the one worth putting Luck of the Sea and Lure on since you will keep it for good.

chain.title: Super Durable
chain.desc: Halves your rod's wear: 50% of casts cost no durability. Pair it with the diamond rod and you can fish for hours without repairs.

chain.title: The Sea's Rarest Catch
chain.desc: A very rare fishing treasure. Place it and open it: alongside kelp and driftwood it holds neptunium ingots or a finished neptunium tool. Everything below depends on farming these.

chain.title: Metal From The Deep
chain.desc: There is no neptunium ore and nothing smelts into it. It comes out of Neptune's Bounty, or as single Neptunium Nuggets straight off the line - nine nuggets to an ingot. Expect a long grind for a full set.

chain.title: Neptune's Song
chain.desc: Fish are more likely to bite while you hold it, which also means faster hunting for more Bounties. The first neptunium item worth making.

chain.title: Neptune's Feast
chain.desc: Cuts more fillets out of each fish than any other knife. If you are feeding a base from the water, this is the piece that pays for itself.

chain.title: Breathe Down There
chain.desc: Lets you breathe underwater with no air bar at all. With the helmet, leggings and boots you also get clear vision, weightlessness and swim speed.

chain.title: The Last Hook
chain.desc: A nether star fused onto a diamond hook: 50% durability saving plus a luck bonus. The endgame hook, and the reason to keep a beacon's worth of stars.

chain.title: Mount The Big One
chain.desc: A wall plaque that displays a single caught fish. Pure trophy, but it is the only place a fish's weight is worth showing off.

collections.note: The remaining craftable hooks, each a different modifier fitted into the same rod slot. Heavy casts shorter, Light casts further, Redstone widens the reel-in window, Note plays an alert when a fish approaches.
Fish species. Which ones bite depends on biome; all of them fillet into the same raw fillet.
The rest of the neptunium set, all crafted from ingots pulled out of Neptune's Bounty.
Wood variants of the fish mount. Decoration only.
Fish buckets. One per water-dwelling species, made by using a bucket on a live fish.

notes:
VERIFIED against the jar named above. Every id here is a key in assets/aquaculture/lang/en_us.json AND has a model in assets/aquaculture/models/item/.

ORDER SOURCE: data/aquaculture/recipes/ plus data/aquaculture/loot_tables/. The mod ships only recipe-unlock advancements (data/aquaculture/advancements/recipes/, 68 of them), so there is no author-authored progression tree to copy; recipes and loot are the whole evidence base.

NEPTUNIUM IS LOOT, NOT A CRAFT. The recipes folder contains neptunium_ingot_from_nuggets, neptunium_ingot_from_neptunium_block and neptunium_nugget only - all re-packing recipes, plus neptunes_bounty.json which crafts eight ingots BACK into a Bounty (a sink, never a source). There are exactly two generative sources, both in data/aquaculture/loot_tables/gameplay/fishing/neptunium.json, whose single pool has three equally weighted entries: a Neptune's Bounty pre-filled from box/neptunes_bounty.json, a straight aquaculture:neptunium_nugget, and a fallthrough to minecraft:gameplay/fishing/treasure (the file's own comments call these '33% chance' each). box/neptunes_bounty.json then rolls one junk entry plus either 1-4 neptunium ingots or one finished neptunium tool/armour/rod/knife. So the nugget route is real: nine nuggets make an ingot. Never write a quest implying neptunium is mined or smelted, and never say the Bounty is the only source.

TREASURE CHEST IS THE RARE ONE. data/aquaculture/loot_tables/gameplay/fishing/junk.json weights: driftwood 10, tin_can 10, seagrass 10, kelp 9, box 6, message_in_a_bottle 5, fish_bones 4, lockbox 4, goldfish 4, treasure_chest 1. An earlier draft called the Treasure Chest 'the common tier' - it is the rarest entry in the pool and the richest of the three containers (box/treasure_chest.json is pure iron/gold/diamond/emerald, weights 40/30/15/15).

FISHING LINE AND BOBBER ARE COSMETIC. com/teammetallurgy/aquaculture/item/DyeableItem.class exists, TackleBoxBlockEntity references DyeableLeatherItem and holds FISHING_LINE and BOBBER slots. A previous version of this chain claimed the fishing line 'adds durability to your cast' - it does not. Durability savings come from hooks only (Hook.durabilityChance in the api/fishing package).

ROD TIERS USE VANILLA Tiers - iron, gold and diamond differ in durability alone, and gold is WORSE than iron. The gold rod is deliberately absent from the chain; an earlier draft claimed it granted a luck bonus, which is wrong. Only the neptunium rod has a special property, and en_us.json states it plainly: 'Fish are more likely to bite'.

HOOK AND NEPTUNIUM EFFECTS in the descs are taken verbatim from the tooltip block of en_us.json (aquaculture.<item>.tooltip.title / .desc), which spells out every effect. Hook.class confirms the backing fields: luckModifier, durabilityChance, doubleCatchChance, weight, fluids.

SIX HOOKS ARE UNOBTAINABLE FROM THIS JAR ALONE: obsidian_hook, double_obsidian_hook, obsidian_note_hook, glowstone_hook, quartz_hook and soul_sand_hook have lang keys, item models and entity textures but NO recipe in data/aquaculture/recipes/, and the nether and lava fishing tables that would supply them (gameplay/fishing/nether/*, gameplay/fishing/lava/*) ship EMPTY. They are excluded from both the chain and the hook collection. Do not generate quests for them unless the pack adds a datapack that fills those tables.

WORMS have no recipe. They come from working grass and dirt, and from the Worm Farm, which eats compostables - the config line 'Should fish be added as compostables for the composter/worm farm?' confirms the farm's input.

FILLETING is data/aquaculture/recipes/fish_fillet.json, type aquaculture:crafting_special_fish_fillet: a fish plus a fillet knife in the crafting grid, not a shaped pattern. Verbs matter here - it is 'cut', not 'craft'.

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT OF THE CHAIN: turtle_soup and the three turtles (fine but marginal), neptunium_block (storage), gold and diamond fillet knives (the ladder reads better as wooden -> iron -> neptunium), message_in_a_bottle, algae, driftwood, tin_can and fish_bones (all junk-pool filler), and aquaculture:farmland, which is a technical block that drops plain dirt.
